packet.headline_seed: US and Iran exchange strikes and accuse each other of violating ceasefire
packet.description_seed: Iran says it has launched retaliatory attacks at US infrastructure in Kuwait and Bahrain after the US said it hit multiple targets across Iran.

what: US and Iran exchange strikes and accuse each other of violating ceasefire

clean_source_blocks.text: The US has conducted new strikes on Iran, following a drone attack on a Panama-flagged vessel in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday. US Central Command (Centcom) said it hit multiple targets across Iran in direct response to "continued aggression" against commercial shipping. In retaliation, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it has launched missiles and drones at US infrastructure in Kuwait and Bahrain, in a statement shared to state media. It warned that violating the ceasefire is against the agreement signed between the two nations and "will lead to a complete halt to the process". Centcom said in a statement, "Iran was given a chance to honor the ceasefire agreement but elected not to when its forces launched a one-way attack drone that hit MT Kiku," a Panama-flagged tanker.
Iran says it has launched retaliatory attacks at US infrastructure in Kuwait and Bahrain after the US said it hit multiple targets across Iran.

Shortly after the latest strikes were announced, the US president took to Truth Social, where he said was it was "very possible" that Tehran would "never learn". "There may come a point when we are no longer able to be reasonable, and will be forced to militarily complete the job that we very successfully started," he wrote on Saturday evening. The post went on: "If that happens, the Islamic Republic of Iran will no longer exist!" In the hours following the US strikes, Kuwait and Bahrain both reported that their air defence systems had been activated. "Kuwaiti air defenses are currently confronting hostile missile and drone attacks," the Kuwaiti Armed Forces said in a statement shared to X, asking the public to adhere to security instructions.

The United States launched military strikes against Iran on Friday following an Iranian drone attack on a commercial cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, further escalating tensions despite a ceasefire agreement reached last week. Both Washington and Tehran accused each other of violating the terms of the truce, raising fresh concerns over stability in the strategically important waterway. According to U.S. Central Command, American aircraft targeted Iranian missile and drone storage facilities, along with coastal radar installations. A U.S. official confirmed the military operation had concluded successfully. Iranian authorities, however, reported that a projectile struck the area near a pier in Sirik, southern Iran, and claimed their naval forces retaliated by attacking U.S. military positions in the region.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
The US has conducted new strikes on Iran, following a drone attack on a Panama-flagged vessel in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday.

US Central Command (Centcom) said it hit multiple targets across Iran in direct response to "continued aggression" against commercial shipping.

In retaliation, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it has launched missiles and drones at US infrastructure in Kuwait and Bahrain, in a statement shared to state media.

It warned that violating the ceasefire is against the agreement signed between the two nations and "will lead to a complete halt to the process".

Centcom said in a statement, "Iran was given a chance to honor the ceasefire agreement but elected not to when its forces launched a one-way attack drone that hit MT Kiku," a Panama-flagged tanker.

In response, it said it had hit military equipment, communication systems, air defense sites and drone storage facilities.

In the IRGC's statement, it said the US had attacked five coastal posts in Iran under what it called "the pretext of the IRGC Navy confronting the offending ship".

It said that under the Memorandum of Understanding signed earlier this month, Iran has arrangements for controlling passage and navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, and from now on, violating ships will be dealt with more forcefully than in the past.

"Any potential enemy aggression, under any pretext, even if the aggressions are against minor targets, as happened last night and tonight, will have a crushing response," read the statement.

Shortly after the latest strikes were announced, the US president took to Truth Social, where he said was it was "very possible" that Tehran would "never learn".

"There may come a point when we are no longer able to be reasonable, and will be forced to militarily complete the job that we very successfully started," he wrote on Saturday evening.

The post went on: "If that happens, the Islamic Republic of Iran will no longer exist!"

In the hours following the US strikes, Kuwait and Bahrain both reported that their air defence systems had been activated.

"Kuwaiti air defenses are currently confronting hostile missile and drone attacks," the Kuwaiti Armed Forces said in a statement shared to X, asking the public to adhere to security instructions.

Bahrain's Ministry of Interior has urged citizens to "remain calm and head to the nearest safe place".

Centcom has said that commercial vessels are continuing to operate in the Strait of Hormuz.

The United States launched military strikes against Iran on Friday following an Iranian drone attack on a commercial cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, further escalating tensions despite a ceasefire agreement reached last week. Both Washington and Tehran accused each other of violating the terms of the truce, raising fresh concerns over stability in the strategically important waterway.

According to U.S. Central Command, American aircraft targeted Iranian missile and drone storage facilities, along with coastal radar installations. A U.S. official confirmed the military operation had concluded successfully. Iranian authorities, however, reported that a projectile struck the area near a pier in Sirik, southern Iran, and claimed their naval forces retaliated by attacking U.S. military positions in the region.

The latest exchange came after Iran warned Gulf nations against supporting Washington and reiterated its intention to oversee traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump blamed Tehran for the drone attack on a commercial vessel near Oman’s coast, calling it a direct breach of the recently signed ceasefire.

In a statement, U.S. Central Command described the strikes as a “powerful response” to what it called an unprovoked assault on international shipping. The military also reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring safe passage for commercial vessels traveling through the vital maritime corridor, where roughly one-fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas supplies pass.

Vice President JD Vance defended the administration’s actions, saying the United States had fully honored the ceasefire agreement, also referred to as a memorandum of understanding. payload.title: Yhdysvallat ja Iran syyttävät toisiaan tulitauon rikkomisesta uusien iskujen jälkeen
payload.summary: Yhdysvallat kertoo iskeneensä useisiin kohteisiin Iranissa Hormuzinsalmen alushyökkäyksen jälkeen. Iran sanoo vastanneensa iskuilla Yhdysvaltain infrastruktuuriin Kuwaitissa ja Bahrainissa.
payload.content:
Yhdysvallat ja Iran syyttävät toisiaan tulitauon rikkomisesta sen jälkeen, kun Yhdysvallat kertoi iskeneensä useisiin kohteisiin Iranissa ja Iran ilmoitti vastanneensa ohjus- ja drooni-iskuilla Yhdysvaltain infrastruktuuriin Kuwaitissa ja Bahrainissa. Tapahtumat ovat kiristäneet tilannetta Hormuzinsalmen alueella, joka on kansainvälisen merenkulun kannalta strategisesti tärkeä väylä.

## Yhdysvallat perusteli iskuja alushyökkäyksellä

Yhdysvaltain keskusjohto Centcomin mukaan iskut tehtiin vastauksena Iranin jatkuneeseen aggressioon kaupallista merenkulkua vastaan. Centcom sanoi Iranin joukkojen tehneen yksisuuntaisella droonilla hyökkäyksen MT Kiku -nimiseen, Panaman lipun alla kulkevaan tankkeriin Hormuzinsalmessa.

Toisen lähteen mukaan Yhdysvaltain koneet kohdistivat iskuja Iranin ohjus- ja droonivarastoihin sekä rannikon tutka-asemiin. Yhdysvaltalaisviranomaisen kerrottiin vahvistaneen, että operaatio oli päättynyt onnistuneesti. Iranilaisviranomaisten mukaan ammus osui alueelle lähelle laituria Sirikissä Etelä-Iranissa.

## Iran sanoo vastanneensa Kuwaitissa ja Bahrainissa

Iranin vallankumouskaarti IRGC ilmoitti valtiollisessa mediassa, että se oli laukaissut ohjuksia ja drooneja Yhdysvaltain infrastruktuuria kohti Kuwaitissa ja Bahrainissa. Iran varoitti, että tulitaukosopimuksen rikkominen voi johtaa prosessin täydelliseen pysähtymiseen.

Kuwait ja Bahrain ilmoittivat Yhdysvaltain iskujen jälkeen, että niiden ilmapuolustusjärjestelmät oli aktivoitu. Kuwaitin asevoimat kertoivat viestipalvelu X:ssä ilmapuolustuksen torjuvan vihamielisiä ohjus- ja droonihyökkäyksiä ja kehottivat yleisöä noudattamaan turvallisuusohjeita.

## Presidentti uhkasi jatkotoimilla

Yhdysvaltain presidentti kommentoi tilannetta Truth Social -palvelussa ja kirjoitti, että on hyvin mahdollista, ettei Teheran koskaan opi. Hän lisäsi, että Yhdysvallat voi joutua sotilaallisesti saattamaan päätökseen työn, jonka se hänen mukaansa aloitti onnistuneesti, jos se ei enää katso voivansa toimia kohtuullisesti.

Sekä Washington että Teheran syyttävät nyt toisiaan tulitauon ehtojen rikkomisesta. Väitteiden ristiriitaisuus ja iskujen leviäminen Iranin ulkopuolisiin kohteisiin lisäävät huolta siitä, että viime viikolla sovittu tulitauko voi horjua nopeasti.
